features.name: Ask about an attached PDF (summary, questions, page questions)
features.use: The person attaches a PDF to a chat and asks for a summary, an answer, or an answer about one page. The product sends the PDF's text, and page images for scanned pages, to the model with the turn.
how_people_use_it: Attach a PDF to the chat composer (click the attach control or drag the file in; exact composer gesture not traced).
Type a request such as 'summarise this' or 'what does page 4 say about fees'.
Send. The answer appears in the chat.
how_it_should_work: Text of each page is marked with a [Page n] label so the model can refer to pages (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:283-292).
Up to 250 pages are read as text. Pages beyond that are flagged as omitted (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:9, 229).
Up to 30 scanned pages are sent as PNG images, with a total image budget of 8 MB (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:10, 16, 252-268).
A file that does not start with the PDF header is refused as unreadable (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:225-227).
A password-protected PDF is refused with a message asking the user to remove the password and upload again (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:44-47, 296-297).
The model is the only summariser; no separate summary code path was found, so summary quality depends on the model.
Limit by plan: not established in the files read.

features.name: Global search dialog and chat history search
features.use: One Search window that finds past chats (by title and by message text), projects, library files, artifacts, code sessions and scheduled tasks, with filters, recent searches and previews.
how_people_use_it: Web and Desktop: open Search from the sidebar or the 'open-search' shortcut.
Type at least 2 characters.
Pick a category chip: All, Artifacts, Sessions, Code, Projects, Scheduled (desktop app also gets 'Local Code').
For All or Sessions, open Filters: message type (all, mine, AI, system), From date, To date, 'Include archived conversations'; 'Clear Filters' resets.
Before typing, click a recent search or a 'frequent search' chip to run it; 'Clear' next to Recent Searches asks for confirmation and then wipes the history.
Click a result to open it.
Mobile: type in the chats list search; searching also covers projects, files, library images and artifacts shown in groups.
CLI: '/sessions search <query>' in the line chat, or 'agi --search <query>' (add --output-format json for all matches).
VS Code: open session history and type in the pick list (2+ characters) or use the sessions sheet search box.
Chrome extension: type in the history drawer search of the side panel.
how_it_should_work: Only the user's own, non-deleted, non-temporary chats are searched; archived ones are left out unless 'include archived' is on.
Search is blocked with a clear message if the workspace's data region cannot be confirmed.
Setting a role or date filter turns off the indexed document search and uses plain row matching only.
Results show title, a snippet with the matched text, and a type label (Title, Project, File, Artifact, Report, Code session, Project source, Scheduled).

Waiting shows a spinner 'Searching workspace'; empty shows 'No results found - Try different keywords or clear filters'; failure shows 'Search could not be completed' with a Retry button; a crash shows 'Search unavailable'.
Each real search is recorded in the user's search history unless the caller asks not to track it.
Mobile on a Cloud account tries the server first and falls back to on-device messages if the server call fails, marking the search as failed; Local mode only searches the phone.
CLI search lists at most 50 most recent sessions and prints a notice when there are more.

features.name: Assistant searches the public web
features.use: A chat can look up current information on the internet and answer with sources; developers using the API can limit which sites it may use.
how_people_use_it: Just ask a question that needs fresh facts; search is automatic where available.

Web/Desktop/Mobile: the composer keeps web search on by itself when the chosen model or service has a search route; asking in words ('search the web for...') or time-bound phrases ('this year', 'who is the current president') makes search required for that turn.
CLI: '/search <question>' makes the next turn a web search; it needs a search key saved with 'agi login' or set in the environment.
VS Code: plus menu 'Set up web search' to save a search key for Local or own-key use.
API: send research_sources.allow_domains and deny_domains with the chat request.
how_it_should_work: Each search returns up to 5 results (title, link, snippet, date when known); at most 3 searches per normal answer and 10 for AGI Work turns; queries over 400 characters are cut.
One retry on a rate limit or server error, 15 second timeout.
Allowed and denied sites (up to 32 each) are passed to the search provider when 20 or fewer, and every result is checked again before the model sees it; a denied site wins over an allowed one.
Results show publication date and retrieval date when known.
If search is unavailable the answer must say so rather than invent sources.
Free plan is limited to 20 search calls per 30 days and the composer blocks sending a search request when the allowance is used up.
Local privacy mode refuses network access.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code and CLI all have web search (CLI and VS Code Local/own-key need the user's own search key; the CLI supports two search services). Site restriction and include/exclude domains exist only in the API; no app screen exposes them. Freshness dates shown on Web, Desktop, Mobile; not CLI, VS Code or Chrome per the brief.

how_it_should_work: Steer needs the run to be active (planning or searching) and have a run id. It is sent to the run's steer endpoint and read by the loop between steps. A person can withdraw a queued steer and send it as a normal message instead.

Pause is requested through the run's pause endpoint; the loop checks it at round boundaries, saves what it gathered as an 'interrupted' report with a paused reason, and emits phase paused. Resume starts a new turn that carries the earlier sources and finished steps, so it does not search from zero.
Cancel (client abort or a durable cancel flag) saves the gathered material as 'interrupted' with 'Research was cancelled.' and sends a stop event with reason cancelled.
If there is no run id the screen says: 'This research cannot be paused. Stop it instead to keep what it found.'
On failure to pause or steer, a toast says the research is still running.

Cancel sets a cancel time on the job; a job already in a provider call finishes or is settled by the next poll; the reservation is released when the job closes as canceled_by_user (cancel/route.ts:60-100; image-job-executor.ts:204-226). A cancelled job is not billed further.
Retry reuses the same prompt and settings in place (ImageGenerationCard.tsx:1076 area; apps/web/app/api/media/image/retry/route.ts).
No partial previews: no preview code was found in apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib.

For a provider that cannot stop a started video, the server records the request, and the result is not delivered and not charged. The message says the provider cannot stop it (cancel route.ts:56-57).
Only one provider has a server-side stop call. It is attempted once and the result is checked afterward (video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:465-490).
If the stop request fails, the placeholder shows an alert with a message and the stop button comes back (MediaGenerationPlaceholder.tsx:276-282, 313-314).
Terminal jobs (completed, failed, outcome unknown) cannot be cancelled. The server returns their current state (cancel route.ts:42-44, 94).

Mobile: tap Read aloud on a reply in the chat; tap again to stop.
Desktop: use the read-aloud action on a reply (desktop steps not traced in detail).
how_it_should_work: Markdown is removed before speaking; code blocks are replaced with a short phrase (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:116-139).
While speaking, the control shows Stop (web: CodeTranscript and message list read isSpeaking; mobile: isSpeaking state in MessageBubble.tsx:1452).
Starting a new reply stops the previous one (useTTS.ts:426-430).
Empty input: nothing is spoken (useTTS.ts:425).
Failure: the message 'Read aloud could not play. Try again.' is shown as a toast (useTTS.ts:12, 68-70).
Server path: input up to 4,000 characters is accepted; the client splits longer text into 3,800-character chunks (useTTS.ts:11, 27-39; speech route.ts:52-56).
Server path limit: 30 requests per minute per user, failing closed (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:404-408).
Local or own-key replies on web: the button is disabled and shows a reason (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3981-3989; apps/web/lib/read-aloud-policy.ts:16-30).
Android with no installed speech voice: the mobile control shows 'No speech voice is installed on this device.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/readAloudAvailability.ts:6-10, 36-38).
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Signed-in replies use the server voice; if the server or audio decode fails on the first chunk, the browser's device voice is used. Desktop: done, per brief; the desktop hook uses native speech commands (apps/desktop/src/hooks/useTTS.ts). Mobile: done. Local mode uses the phone's device voice; Cloud mode uses the server voice and falls back to device voice on failure (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceOutput.ts:114-157). CLI, VS Code, Chrome extension: missing (no speech code found in apps/cli or apps/extension-vscode). API: missing per brief; no separate API app exists.

status_quotes.chrome: Chrome: device voice only, with saved voice and rate; one reply at a time

features.name: Permission modes
features.use: One switch decides how every tool runs: ask every time, run reads without asking, or skip approvals. Read-only and ask-before-writing are variants of the same idea.

how_it_should_work: Ask before every action (ask_every_time) is the default. Reads, searches, page fetches and sandboxed code run on their own under the read-only mode; writes, sends, purchases and unknown tools still ask.
Skip approvals (autonomous) runs tools without waiting, but destructive actions, unknown connector tools and some sends still ask. It is only used when the workspace allows it.
Read-only mode should refuse write, send and execute tools. The code I opened only sets saved levels per tool in the connector panel; it does not refuse them globally (not verified).

features.name: Steer, pause, resume and stop

how_it_should_work: Steer: the message is queued on the run. If the queue is full the request fails (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2850). A message the task can still read cannot be withdrawn; the server says it stays queued (steer/[steerId]/route.ts withdraw error).

Pause: allowed only while the run is in an executor-held state; otherwise HTTP 409 with the text Only a task that is still working can be paused (pause/route.ts). The pause is recorded and the run stops at a step boundary (step boundary not traced).
Cancel: marks cancellation on the server (runs/[runId]/route.ts:81). A run waiting on the person is cancelled at once (route.ts:84 cancelHumanHeldCloudAgentRun).
Resume: a paused run resumes from its checkpoint (resume route).
Failure: each route returns an error; the steer box keeps the draft and shows the error.

features.name: Agent teams, delegation and coordinator
features.use: Run several agents on one job. A lead agent hands work to teammates or one-off specialist subagents and gets the results back. Agents can message each other.

how_it_should_work: Team off: spawn_teammate refuses with 'Agent teams are off. Start agi with --team or AGI_TEAM=1.' Only the lead can spawn teammates.
The names lead and user are reserved. Names must pass a strict safe-character check.

A message to an unknown or stopped teammate fails with a clear error. Messages from other agents are labelled 'another agent on your team, not the person', and the teammate is told they never count as the person's approval.
Each teammate runs in its own thread with its own session. It reports to the lead when it finishes, or if it could not start.
The shared task list has the states pending, in progress, completed, blocked, with dependencies.

A named specialist can only narrow the parent's authority. Its model and permission-mode overrides are ignored, tool lists are intersected with the parent's, deny lists are joined, and max turns can only go down.
Limit: the lead's tool catalog for the agent tool lists at most 200 agents and about 18 KB, and hides prompt bodies, paths, model and permission mode.

features.use: When an agent needs a decision or approval, it stops and asks the person, and the person gets told even when away from the screen.

how_it_should_work: The agent waits for the answer.
Server side, an event of approval_required, input_required, completed or failed writes a feed notification and sends a push. Run finished and failed alerts are de-duplicated per run.
Mobile alerts can be turned off by an explicit false in the mobilePushAgentActivity preference. The default is on.

features.name: Event triggers and webhooks
features.use: Start a routine when something happens outside: a GitHub event, a Slack message, a new Gmail email, a Calendar change, or a signed POST to a URL the routine owns. A documented API call can also start a run.
how_people_use_it: Open a routine, then the Triggers panel (web/desktop), the Triggers screen (mobile) or agi schedules triggers add (CLI).
Choose source (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, or 'Anything else (signed webhook)').
Fill the account (repository, Slack team id, mailbox) and optionally event types.
Optionally add field conditions (narrow by data) and a repeat-suppression wait.
Save. For a webhook the screen shows a URL and a signing secret once. For Slack it shows a verification code to post in the workspace.

how_it_should_work: The webhook URL accepts POSTs of up to 128 KB that carry headers x-agi-timestamp and x-agi-signature (sha256 HMAC of timestamp.body). A bad or old signature returns 401. A missing server key returns 503 (webhooks/connectors/[triggerId]/route.ts:46-100).
Body must be a JSON object with an id (delivery id) and a type.
An event only reaches a trigger if its owner holds the source account (GitHub installation, Slack workspace). Up to 20 triggers per event (trigger-ingest.ts:28).
Conditions and a debounce window can filter out events. Each outcome (filtered, debounced, enqueued, duplicate, failed) is recorded.
A matching event is queued as a job; the job fires the run with the event data appended to the prompt as untrusted data (promptWithEventContext).
Event fire limits: 30 per hour and 720 per day (PLATFORM_EVENT_TRIGGER_RUNS_PER_HOUR/DAY).
If the routine is paused or deleted before the job starts, the delivery is marked filtered with the reason.
A routine of type event has no clock time; clock fields, day-parts and a watch condition are refused for it.
API trigger: the runs endpoint is documented in openapi.json at /schedules/{id}/runs and uses bearer auth; a run needs an Idempotency-Key header.

features.name: Desktop app pairing and connection status
features.use: Connect the extension to the AGI desktop app on the same computer, see whether it is connected, and reconnect.
how_people_use_it: Open the extension Options page, Destinations section, and find the desktop pairing rows (destinations.ts:110; desktop-pairing-rows.ts).

Paste the bridge token from the desktop app if one is set, or follow the code shown by the desktop app: pairing asks the desktop app for a request, the person types the code, and the extension confirms.
In the side panel, a notice Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected appears when the desktop is not connected, with a Reconnect button (side_panel.ts:15637-15648, 9851-9862).

Desktop side: the web app pairing page shows whether the extension is paired, and a link to install the extension (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPairingSection.tsx:120-150). Desktop bridge routes handle pair request and confirm (apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts:410-440).
how_it_should_work: Pairing works only with a local bridge: the address must be localhost or another allowed local host, otherwise the extension says Pairing is only supported with local desktop bridge (pairing.ts:318-332; policy.ts:315-326).
Pairing has phases: idle, requesting, awaiting code, confirming, paired, or error (pairing.ts:1-11).
A failed pairing shows the error text and stays in the error phase (pairing.ts:66-69).
The side panel only reads the status with GET_CONNECTION_STATUS, which may try to connect at most once on a worker start (background.ts:5074-5088).

Reconnect uses exponential back-off from 1 s up to 30 s, for at most 8 attempts; after that only a manual reconnect starts it again (features/native-bridge/reconnect.ts:1-17). Permanent errors such as host not found stop retries at once (reconnect.ts:10-17).
Unpair asks the desktop app to remove the pairing; if the desktop cannot be reached the pairing is kept and the person is asked to try again (background.ts:5114-5122).

CLI: it reads whether a browser is paired from the desktop shell (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:339-345, 1100-1110). Chrome extension: the pairing UI is on Options and the status notice is in the side panel. Status per the brief: desktop done, CLI done, Chrome done.

features.name: Who may use what, and where it runs
features.use: Decides whether a feature, model or route is allowed for this user on this surface. It combines the plan, workspace policy, role, region and age or eligibility rules. It also lets the user pick where a request runs: on the device with a local model, with the user's own provider key, or on the managed cloud.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker or processing-path choice on the composer and pick Local, own key or Cloud (desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code).
Open workspace settings (owner or admin) to set feature switches, model policy and retention.
On web, open Privacy settings to turn the US-only routing option on or off.
On sign-up, accept the terms; on mobile, enter an age at first run.
how_it_should_work: Every gated feature is checked again on the server for each route that runs a model, not only in the UI.
If a plan or policy blocks a model, the UI hides or disables it and the server refuses it with a reason.
Empty or unknown state: a capability the server does not mention stays as the build shipped it (mobile), so an unreachable server does not disable working features.
Failure: a failed read of training opt-out or region data falls back to the stricter routing (the server logs a warning and routes only to models that keep inputs out of training).
Limits by plan: the plan decides the model roster (see the managed auto-routing mapping), and free users get the free model and region rules.

CLI: done, mapping plan to routing tier. VS Code: done for model picker and tier revalidation. Chrome: done for the gating checks (routing and processing-path choice is listed as not applicable in the brief for chrome). Required-connection and age-gate rows differ by app (see other features).

features.name: Auto picks the model
features.use: Auto chooses one model and one provider route per message, so the person does not have to. It only chooses among models the person is allowed to use and can afford.
how_people_use_it: Open the model picker and choose Auto (the default).
Type and send. Nothing else to do.
In the CLI, run agi --auto (Cloud sessions only).
how_it_should_work: Candidates are filtered first: model must be live, not retired, allowed for the plan tier, allowed by workspace policy, allowed in the region, and have a usable credential (evaluateEligibility in auto.ts, around line 1340).
Then candidates are ranked. When one model has several provider routes, one route is chosen by health, cost and cache reuse (slotRouteCost and rankRoutes in auto.ts).

If the person has a credit budget, models whose estimated cost is above the remaining credits are dropped (isAffordable, auto.ts:1682). If the balance cannot be read, routing goes on without this check (request-processor.ts:4607-4612).
A task family such as code or research gives a named profile (Instant, High, Code, Research) that weighs quality, cost and speed (packages/ai/routing/src/profiles/index.ts).
If no route works, the result is an 'unavailable' decision with reasons, not a silent guess.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop (shows the hosted web app) and the public API use the server router in the chat completions route. Mobile and Chrome run the same shared router on the device before sending (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/cloudDispatchRouting.ts, apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatRouting.ts). The CLI uses a Rust version through the model registry crate (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:667-740). VS Code has Auto rows in its picker (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:441-460). Brief status: done on all.

features.name: Understanding the request
features.use: Each message is labelled by kind (coding, research, agentic, image-bearing, long and so on) so routing can match a model to the work.
how_people_use_it: Nothing to do. Type normally, attach images, or switch on Research, Code or Work toggles.
how_it_should_work: A word-pattern classifier looks at the text, attachments and token count (classifyTaskLocally in classify.ts). It forces long-context past a token budget and sends images to multimodal models.
Explicit toggles override the text: research on gives research; Work mode or office creation gives agentic; code execution gives coding (resolveToolAwareTaskType, request-processor.ts:1032-1043).
A second step groups the request into a 'task family' from structural signals; if the signals are unclear it returns no family and the normal Auto policy runs unchanged (task-family.ts:160-200).
Words like 'latest' or 'today' count as research signals (RE_RESEARCH in classify.ts).
There is no model-based classifier: confidence is advisory and routing uses the type only (classify.ts header). If nothing matches, a default general type is used.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop and API classify on the server. Mobile, Chrome and VS Code import the same TypeScript classifier (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/routingTask.ts:1,19). The CLI has a hand-kept Rust copy (apps/cli/src/routing/classify.rs) that tests keep in step. All marked done.

Suspended account: the blocked screen shows an appeal form (email field only when signed out).
how_it_should_work: Content reports reach the content_reports table; the route is an alias of the mobile route.
Copyright notices are stored in public.copyright_notices and never take content down; removal is a separate admin action.
A signed-out appeal needs a human check (bot challenge) and runs after the response is sent.
A signed-in appeal creates a support ticket and sends the user a copy by email. The user can follow it in the appeal thread.
A suspended account with no email on file cannot appeal; the user is told so.

features.name: Sign-in and account standing
features.use: Turns a verified sign-in into one AGI account and blocks any request from an account that is locked, recovering, suspended, banned, scheduled for deletion, or deleted.
how_people_use_it: Sign in through the hosted identity provider (the only provider the code can select).
If the account is locked or suspended, the API returns a denial with a recovery or appeal path instead of the data.
No direct control: the check runs on every request.
how_it_should_work: Every request resolves its identity to one account id; a cached answer is used first, otherwise the database is read, and a new identity row is linked if none exists (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:180-212).
An erased account is refused as erased, not as unknown.

Denial reasons: locked, recovery, suspended, deleted. A lockout points to password reset, a suspension points to the appeal page, and deletion has no recovery path (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).
An account with a scheduled deletion is still allowed, so the person can cancel it while signed in (account-status.ts:68-70).
Failure: if the account-status lookup takes longer than its deadline, the workspace binding fails rather than passing the request (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:225-229).
No plan limits seen.
features.on_each_app: Server only, in the web app's API layer. Desktop, mobile, CLI and extension reach it through the same API. The brief marks it done on the platform; no per-app behaviour is recorded.

features.name: Sessions and device sign-in credentials
features.use: Lets a person see which sessions and devices are signed in, end some or all of them, and keep device sign-in alive safely with rotating refresh tokens.
how_people_use_it: Open the sessions list (GET /api/settings/sessions) and see active sessions.
Sign out everything else (DELETE /api/settings/sessions revokes all other sessions, per the handler at apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:189-199).
Open the device list (GET /api/settings/devices), rename a device (PATCH /api/settings/devices/{deviceId}), unlink a device (DELETE on the same route), or stop remote work on it (POST).
A device keeps itself registered by sending heartbeats (POST /api/devices/heartbeat).
how_it_should_work: Session listing returns a bounded page with a truncation flag and a count of sessions that ended by lifetime rules (sessions/route.ts:178-186).
Revoking all sessions is rate-limited and needs a CSRF token and a step-up check before it runs (sessions/route.ts:189-198).

Device refresh rotates a token each time. A token used a second time is a replay: the whole family is marked compromised and revoked, and a compromise record is written (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:305-328).
A device refresh is withheld with a terms error (403) until current terms are accepted, or an age-review error until an adult decision exists (device/refresh/route.ts:257-279).
Heartbeat never turns remote work back on by itself; only pairing again turns it on (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:21-23).
Failure: a provider rate limit makes the bulk session revoke wait and retry, up to a fixed attempt limit (apps/web/lib/server/session-revocation.ts:127-139), then reports what failed.
Developer tokens are revoked by writing their id into a revoked list (apps/web/lib/server/developer-token.ts:135-144).
features.on_each_app: Web server endpoints are shared. The mobile store and the CLI remote-control module call the pairing and device flow (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts:960-994; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:180-201). Desktop and the others are not traced in this brief.

Support staff open the ticket and choose an action (POST /api/support/staff/tickets/{ticketId}/recovery) to remove the second factor or add a new sign-in email.
how_it_should_work: A request for an unknown email, or for a deleted account, does nothing visible, so the form does not reveal which accounts exist (apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts:39-49).
If the account has advanced security enrolled, the request is logged as an event instead of a ticket (recovery.ts:51-59).
Otherwise a ticket is opened and the requester gets a receipt email (recovery.ts:69-98).
Staff may only act on a recovery ticket that is still open, and never on an account with advanced security enrolled; that account's owner must use a recovery key (recovery.ts:116-126).
Each change emits a security event (recovery.ts:139-144).
Failure: a ticket error returns a validation message to staff; a missing ticket returns not found (staff recovery route).

features.name: Pairing a second device
features.use: Links a phone or another desktop to a signed-in desktop or account with a short code, so the second device can use remote control.
how_people_use_it: The desktop or account creates a code and shows it as a QR code (POST /api/pair/initiate returns qrData 'agiw:<code>').
The phone scans or types the code and claims it (POST /api/pair/claim), which sends the account id to the relay.
The phone app then connects using the pairing secret it was given (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts:960-994).
how_it_should_work: Initiating needs a signed-in person, a CSRF token, a rate limit, and a current remote-control standing check (pair/initiate/route.ts:47-66).
If the relay URL or its secret is missing, the request returns 503 'Pairing is not configured' rather than working without the relay (pair/initiate/route.ts:69-80).
Relay URLs must be secure, except localhost in development (pair/initiate/route.ts:72).
Claim sends the account id to the relay, and the relay rejects a rotation that does not match the stored account id (services/signaling-server/src/db.ts:170-177).
A pairing expires; the relay sweeps expired pairings about an hour after they expire, so the maximum age is eight days (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:425-435).
Desktop-side pairing codes are 8 characters and relay codes 12 characters (packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts:50-60).
Failure: an unreachable relay during claim is logged and reported (pair/claim route).
features.on_each_app: Web server (pair routes), relay service (services/signaling-server), mobile app (apps/mobile/stores/connectionStore.ts), and the CLI remote-control module (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:190-201, which checks the server address). Desktop uses the same contract types.

features.name: Sync between devices
features.use: Keeps chats, messages and artifacts the same on every device. A change made offline is queued and sent when the connection returns. A delete reaches the other devices and stays deleted.
how_people_use_it: Make a change on the phone, then open the web app or the CLI. The change is there.
Go offline, make edits, then come back online. The app sends the queued changes and shows the server copy if a conflict is found.
Delete a chat on one device. It disappears from the others.
how_it_should_work: Each device pulls changes since its last cursor and pushes its own changes with a base version. The server applies a change when the base version matches, treats an identical repeat as done, and returns a conflict with the server copy otherwise (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:235-259; 310-320; 334-355).

Every change, including a soft delete, gets a new server_version from a sequence through a trigger (apps/web/db/neon/0038_cloud_sync_versioning.sql:50-62). Deletes are sent as tombstones (packages/client/sync/src/conversations.ts:52-55).

A delete pushed by a device is not re-created by a later push of the same chat: the server only applies a push when the row is not deleted or the push is also a delete (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:629 and 833).

The pull returns at most 500 chats, 1000 messages and 500 artifacts per call (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:54-56). The cursor is moved to the lowest version that was not fully returned (route.ts:974-1000).

Protocol version: a push that declares a version the server cannot read is refused with 426 (update required) when it is too old, and with a validation error when it is too new (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:940-947; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/sync.ts:33-43).

The mobile app syncs every 30 seconds while active and again when it comes back to the foreground (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1068-1077). Its queue of changes is kept on the phone (apps/mobile/stores/chat/cloudSyncStateStore.ts:88-96).

The CLI records server versions after each push and pull (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs:343-364). Its handshake reads the 426 status and the minimum version header (apps/cli/src/cloud/handshake.rs:31-60).
A sync push is refused for a temporary chat on mobile (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1088-1094).

features.name: Running tools in a turn
features.use: Runs the model, then its tool calls, then the model again, until the answer is done or a limit is hit. Read-only calls can run side by side; anything that changes state runs one at a time. Cancelling stops the stream and the tools in flight.
how_people_use_it: Send a message in chat; the answer shows each tool step as it runs.
Press stop (or cancel the run) to end the turn.
Approve or reject calls that need it (see approvals feature).
how_it_should_work: The loop repeats until the model is finished or the step limit is reached. At the limit the run pauses with a checkpoint and continues only if a resume raises the limit.
Up to 4 read-only calls run at once in the main loop; the research loop allows 3.
Any call that is not declared read-only, and every undeclared connector tool, runs one at a time.
Each result is capped in size and wrapped as untrusted data; a tool error is wrapped too and marked as an error.
Cancel: the model stream and in-flight tools are stopped and the turn is settled as cancelled.
A turn is treated as empty, blocked, cancelled or cut off by one shared set of checks.
Dependency-aware ordering: not applicable (no code found).
Empty state: a turn with no text and no tool output counts as an empty turn.
Failure: a timed-out tool returns a timeout message to the model; an empty provider step can trigger a failover to another route.

Pending requests are stored with the exact calls and messages, so a decision on another device can resume the run.
A decision applies only to the calls it was made for; stale or mismatched decisions are refused.
Each decision is recorded per call, and the checkpoint is claimed under a short lease.
Failure: a checkpoint that does not match the event history is refused.

features.name: Learn facts from chats
features.use: After an ordinary chat turn, the server pulls short personal facts out of the user's message and saves them as memories, merging duplicates and letting a newer contradicting fact replace an older one. Each saved memory records its source chat, turn and writer.
how_people_use_it: Chat normally, e.g. state a fact in a sentence that is not a question.
Nothing else to do: the memory is saved after the reply, unless the chat is temporary, the account has learning off, or the request is from the API surface.
To see where a memory came from, open it in Settings > Memory (source chat and writer are stored with it).
how_it_should_work: Only statements, not questions, and not task-only reminders ('remember this tab id' style runtime notes) become candidates; at most 5 candidates are taken per turn.
Learning is blocked for temporary chats, the API surface, when the per-chat memory override is off, when the workspace has memory off, or when the account's generate-from-history flag is off.

Duplicate wording (for example 'my favorite color is teal' vs 'the user's favorite color is teal') is matched by a normalized key and merged, not stored twice; a merge keeps the stronger expiry and pin.
A newer fact on the same topic supersedes the older one (superseded_by is set so the old one stops being read).

A refused upload's bytes are deleted, not moved to a quarantine area (chat-attachment-completion.ts:414).

features.name: Limits, rate and spend controls
features.use: Stops a person or workspace from using more than the plan or budget allows, by rolling windows, rate, concurrent responses and monthly spend.
how_people_use_it: Send messages normally. When a limit is hit the reply says so and names the window (for example the 5-hour or weekly limit) and the reset point.
Admins set a monthly spend limit for a workspace; when the limit is reached managed usage stops until the owner raises it or the month resets.
Sending a message while the plan's concurrent-response count is full gets a message to stop or wait.
how_it_should_work: Each managed request is checked against plan limits before the model runs. Refusal texts exist for session_limit (rolling 5-hour), weekly_limit, flagship_weekly_limit and declined (monthly) (managed-usage-request-service.ts:440-467).
Daily free caps and monthly metered units come from the tier policy (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:50-75).
Rate limits are shared across instances through the rate limiter, and the limit can depend on the plan tier (rate-limit.ts:961, 1234-1250).
Concurrent responses use a slot per turn. A plan with no concurrency gets a refusal; if the limiter itself is unavailable the reply is HTTP 503 with Retry-After 30 (turn-slot.ts:20-40).
A workspace with a block-mode monthly cap refuses new managed usage with code over_cap (spend-limit-service.ts:175-184).
Limit numbers are configuration from the plan, not constants in the feature.
features.on_each_app: Enforcement is server-side on the managed Cloud path, so every app that calls it gets the same limits. Per-app messages are not verified.

features.name: Metered usage ledger (reserve, settle, release, cost)
features.use: Records each metered model call in a durable ledger. Before a call the estimated cost is held (reserved). After the call the hold is replaced by the real cost. Failed or stranded holds are released.
how_people_use_it: Nothing visible in the normal flow: a message is sent and the cost is taken from the plan window or usage credits.
On a failed reply the hold is released and the person is not charged for it.
Usage credits can be used for extra usage when turned on (usageCreditsEnabled, managed-usage-request-service.ts:715).
how_it_should_work: Reservation takes a parsed idempotency key, the estimated cost, the plan's session and weekly caps, and writes through a database function (managed-usage-request-service.ts:738-827).
Finalization sets the billed amount and the provider cost separately; a failed outcome records zero cost for both (managed-usage-request-service.ts:1140-1170).
Stranded reservations are recovered by a cron job, which releases them and drains the settlement queue; the job is skipped in low-power mode (cron/recover-reservations/route.ts:20-60).
Cost is attributed to user, organization, conversation, API key, schedule run and artifact subject (managed-usage-request-service.ts:614-712).
An artifact (published app) can be capped per app and cannot be billed to usage credits (managed-usage-request-service.ts:763-769).
features.on_each_app: Server-side for all managed calls. The brief gives no per-app difference.

features.name: Shared request and response shapes

how_people_use_it: A person does not touch this directly.

how_it_should_work: Every client-called route and every client parses its body with the shared schema. The brief says this is partial: 164 routes still lack one (settings 50, admin 30 and smaller families), and the connector routes for bank accounts, exchange and link still fail the route-contract check.

features.name: Sign-in, API and streaming clients
features.use: One shared sign-in client (device sign-in: start, poll, refresh, approve), one API client for server calls, and one streaming reader (server-sent events) with reconnect.

The token route can answer pending, slow-down, denied, expired, invalid, account-unavailable or terms-acceptance-required (device-authorization.ts:55-73). A refusal that asks for terms or age review must send the person to the review page at the acceptance URL (device-authorization.ts:61-72).

Stream reads must reconnect after a drop and must not show a run as finished when only the connection dropped. The brief marks this done; the Mobile implementation is apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts.
VS Code and Chrome send idempotency keys on chat, schedule and cloud run calls (brief). The Electron main process does not use the shared managed-cloud client.

features.use: One reducer for conversation state (activity, queue, message status), one sync engine (cursors, pushes, pulls, tombstones, conflicts), and one task and run lifecycle vocabulary.

A scheduled run that is partial or timed out must count as finished (the brief says Chrome now treats both as terminal).

features.name: Durable agent runs and deep research
features.use: A long agent turn or a deep research run is handed to a durable workflow, so it keeps going after the browser request has ended. Stuck runs are cleaned up by a reaper.
how_people_use_it: Start a task that needs many steps, or switch on deep research for a question.
Close the tab and come back later; the run continues on the server.
Cancel a run from the chat (the server checks for a cancellation request).
how_it_should_work: A turn starts a workflow run on the queue named cloud-agent-turn (apps/web/lib/workflows/start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:63; runCloudAgentTurn at :264).
The workflow loops over steps: wait for a device if one is needed, run one invocation, settle the work plan, close the stream (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts:69-100).
If a device is asleep the workflow waits up to 60 minutes, then removes the device tools and continues (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:14-16).
A reaper cron finds orphaned runs and ends them (apps/web/app/api/cron/reap-agent-runs/route.ts:23; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:90). It runs on the schedule in vercel.json.
Deep research: a bounded loop of plan, search and fetch rounds, then a cited answer (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/research-loop.ts, fetch step near :2767). Free users are refused.
Failure: a failed run is marked failed and its stream closed (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:55-62).
features.on_each_app: Platform status is done. The server runs these for the web app and for any surface that starts a cloud agent turn. The brief does not give per-app differences.
